subject: Result of Fisher Exact Test and qValue

messages.author: ae74e91a21b6b199
messages.subject: Result of Fisher Exact Test and qValue
parts:
Hello,

In some samples calculateDiffMeth function calculates p as zero and q value could be calculated as negative. It seems a bit strange to me. It may not be a big problem since both cases we can reject null hypothesis but I'll be pleased if anyone could tell me is there something wrong  or may be I miss something linked to default multiple test correction method of methylkit. Finally do you think is it ok to write a negative q Value to a paper or saying q >0.01 makes more sense.

Thanks,

Serbulent

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Result of Fisher Exact Test and qValue
parts:
it is not expected to have negative q-values, p-values may appear as zero due to machine precision. If you are using the latest methylKit change use adjust="qvalue" method and see if it helps. If you are worried send a reproducible example. How you should present the statistics depends on journal policies, they might be OK with saying "q-value < 0.01"

Best,
Altuna
